SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p432/r1.claim: Tin adds fa before the reward because its context does not explicitly identify the people returned low, while al-Inshiqaq describes disbelievers at length and its believers briefly, making omission of fa suit that brevity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p432/r1.anchor: ثم انظر كيف زاد الفاء في قوله (فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p433/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p433/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p433/r1.claim: Al-Inshiqaq begins with human toil and successive hardships, whereas Tin begins by honoring humanity; this makes the added fa fit the affirmation that the reward continues without being marred.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p433/r1.anchor: في حين بدأ في سورة التين بتكريم الإنسان فقال (لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ (4) التين) فناسب ذلك تأكيد استمرار أجره وعدم تنغيصه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r2.claim: On that reading, verse 6 promises that older believers who did good deeds retain uninterrupted reward and spiritual progress despite bodily and mental decline.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r2.anchor: inanıp iyi işler yapan yaşlı kimselerin, itaatlerinden dolayı kesintisiz ödül alacaklarını, bedenen ve zihnen gerileseler bile mânen ilerleyeceklerini ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r4.claim: The commentary's preferred reading is that unbelievers who fail to do righteous deeds misuse their God-given potential and regress instead of developing and earning reward.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r4.anchor: İman etmeyen ve sâlih amel (iyi, erdemli, dünya ve âhiret için yararlı işler) yapmayan kimseler, Allah Teâlâ’nın insana verdiği

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p429/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p429/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p429/r1.claim: After excluding believers from being cast low, the text adds a tremendous reward; the indefinite form magnifies it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p429/r1.anchor: وفرع على معنى الاستثناء وهو أنهم ليسوا ممن يرد أسفل سافلين الإخبار بأن لهم أجرا عظيما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p429/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p429/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p429/r2.claim: Mamnun can mean an unblemished reward on which no one reproaches the recipient, or a reward that is not cut off, from the word for severed rope.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p429/r2.anchor: والممنون : الذي يمن على المأجور به

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r1.claim: One interpretation of the preceding phrase says the reward is uncounted.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r2.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r2.claim: Another interpretation says the reward is not spoiled by reproach or injury.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r2.anchor: الثالث : غير مكدر بالمن والأذى , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r3.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r3.claim: Another interpretation says the reward is not cut off.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r3.anchor: الرابع : غير مقطوع , قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r4.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r4.claim: Another interpretation says it is reward without prior work.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r4.anchor: الخامس : أجر بغير عمل , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r5.claim: A report says that someone who reaches old age is credited with the reward for good deeds he can no longer perform.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r6.claim: He says whatever one does in old age does not harm him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p302/r6.anchor: أن لا يضر كل أحد منهم ما عمله في كبره , قاله ابن مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.claim: Surat al-Tin is also called al-Tin without the conjunction; most say it is Meccan, while Qatada and a report from Ibn Abbas call it Medinan. The reference to the secure city is unanimously taken as Mecca, supporting the majority; all agree on eight verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.anchor: ويقال لها سورة التين بلا واو مكية في قول الجمهور وعن قتادة أنها مدنية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.claim: After the preceding surah described Muhammad as the most perfect human, this surah discusses humanity's condition and end and God's reward for those who follow that exemplary figure.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.anchor: لما ذكر سبحانه في السورة السابقة حال أكمل النوع الإنساني بالإتفاق بل أكمل خلق الله

ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r2.claim: On the senility interpretation, the pen is lifted from a believer and the exception is disconnected; not everyone is afflicted, only some in the human kind.
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r2.anchor: أما المؤمن فمرفوع عنه القلم والاستثناء على هذا منقطع ، وليس المعنى أن كل إنسان يعتريه هذا

ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r3.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو العالية وابن زيد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r3.claim: Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliya, Ibn Zayd, and Qatada also say it means the disbeliever is cast into Hell; on this reading the exception is connected.
ABUHAYYAN:95:5/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد وأبو العالية وابن زيد وقتادة أيضا : { أسفل سافلين } في النار على كفره ، ثم استثنى

ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r1.claim: If the return is to senility, righteous elderly people still receive lasting reward for obedience and for patiently enduring God's trial of old age.
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r1.anchor: وعلى أن ذلك الرد هو إلى الهرم ، فالمعنى : ولكن الصالحين من الهرمى لهم ثواب دائم غير منقطع على طاعتهم

ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r2.claim: A hadith says that one who reaches a hundred without acting is credited with the deeds he did in health and has no sin recorded against him; no authority is named.
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r2.anchor: إذا بلغ مائة ولم يعمل كتب له مثل ما كان يعمل في صحته

ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r3.claim: Another hadith says a believer reduced to extreme old age is credited with the deeds he performed in his strength; no authority is named.
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r3.anchor: أن المؤمن إذا رد لأرذل العمر كتب له ما كان يعمل في قوته

ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan glosses the reward as uninterrupted and uncut, also mentioning the sense of a counted favor bestowed on them.
ABUHAYYAN:95:6/r4.anchor: وذلك أجر غير ممنون وممنوع مقطوع ، أي محسوب يمن به عليهم

ALUSI:95:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:6/r1.claim: On the preceding interpretation, the exception connects to the pronoun in raddadnahu, which collectively denotes humankind; believers are not made ugly at resurrection but gain added beauty.
ALUSI:95:6/r1.anchor: على ما تقدم استثناء متصل من ضمير

ALUSI:95:6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:6/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:6/r2.claim: Ghayru mamnun means either an unending reward or one not held over believers as a favor.
ALUSI:95:6/r2.anchor: أي غير مقطوع أو غير ممنون به عليهم

ALUSI:95:6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:6/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:6/r3.claim: The reward statement confirms that believers escape the preceding fate and clarifies their state; on the second gloss the exception is disconnected and means rather or but.
ALUSI:95:6/r3.anchor: مقرر لما يفيده الاستثناء من خروجهم عن حكم الرد ومبين لكيفية حالهم

ALUSI:95:6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:6/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI:95:6/r4.claim: Some scholars call the exception disconnected because its purpose is not to remove believers from the old-age ruling; disconnectedness depends on intended ruling, not literal inclusion or exclusion.
ALUSI:95:6/r4.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين الانقطاع لأنه لم يقصد إخراجهم من الحكم وهو مدار الاتصال والانقطاع

ALUSI:95:6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:6/r5.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI:95:6/r5.claim: Several interpreters understand the believers as righteous people who reach old age and receive continuing reward for patiently enduring age-related inability to perform devotional duties.
ALUSI:95:6/r5.anchor: وحمل غير واحد هؤلاء المؤمنين على الصالحين من الهرمي كأنه قيل لكن الذين كانوا صالحين من الهرمي لهم ثواب دائم

ALUSI:95:6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:6/r6.speaker: أبو موسى
ALUSI:95:6/r6.claim: The Prophet says that when a servant is ill or traveling, God records the reward of the deeds he used to do while healthy and resident; another version says he recited this verse.
ALUSI:95:6/r6.anchor: أخرج أحمد والبخاري وابن حبان عن أبي موسى قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:95:6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:6/r7.speaker: شداد بن أوس
ALUSI:95:6/r7.claim: Shaddad reports a divine saying: a tested believer who praises God rises cleansed of sins, and God orders that his prior healthy reward be recorded for him.
ALUSI:95:6/r7.anchor: أخرج الطبراني عن شداد بن أوس قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:95:6/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:6/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:95:6/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when an aging servant weakens and cannot work, he is credited with the reward of what he did in youth.
ALUSI:95:6/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال في الآية إذا كبر العبد وضعف عن العمل كتب له أجر ما كان يعمل في شبيبته

ALUSI:95:6/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:6/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:95:6/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says Quran reciters are not returned to decrepit age and reads the exception as those who recited the Quran; al-Hakim authenticated the report and al-Bayhaqi included it in Shuʿab.
ALUSI:95:6/r9.anchor: عن الحبر قال من قرأ القرآن لم يرد إلى أرذل العمر وذلك قوله تعالى ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين إلا الذين آمنوا

ALUSI:95:6/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:6/r10.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI:95:6/r10.claim: Ikrima similarly says Quran reciters do not fall into the state of knowing nothing after having knowledge.
ALUSI:95:6/r10.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير عن عكرمة نحوه وفيه أنه لا ينزل تلك المنزلة يعني الهرم كي لا يعلم من بعد علم شيئاً

ALUSI:95:6/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:6/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:6/r11.claim: Al-Alusi says restricting all believers here to Quran reciters is contrary to the apparent meaning, and doubts that no Quran reciter ever reaches decrepit age.
ALUSI:95:6/r11.anchor: ولا يخفى أن تخصيص الذين آمنوا بما خصص به خلاف الظاهر وفي كون أحد من القراء لا يرد إلى أرذل العمر توقف

BAGHAWI:95:6/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:6/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:95:6/r1.claim: On the Fire interpretation of the previous verse, believers are excepted and are not returned to the Fire.

BAGHAWI:95:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:6/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:95:6/r2.claim: On the old-age interpretation, minds and deeds cease; believers continue receiving credit after senility for the righteous deeds they used to do when young and healthy.
BAGHAWI:95:6/r2.anchor: فإنه يكتب لهم بعد الهرم والخرف ،   مثل الذين كانوا يعملون في حال الشباب والصحة

BAGHAWI:95:6/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:95:6/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says some people in the Prophet's time reached the most decrepit age, and revelation excused them by preserving the reward earned before their minds failed.
BAGHAWI:95:6/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هم نفر ردوا إلى أرذل العمر

BAGHAWI:95:6/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:6/r4.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI:95:6/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says old age did not harm the man because God ended his life upon the best deeds he had performed.
BAGHAWI:95:6/r4.anchor: قال عكرمة : لم يضر هذا الشيخ كبره

BAGHAWI:95:6/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:6/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:95:6/r5.claim: A report through ʿIkrima attributes to Ibn ʿAbbās the view that the exception means those who read the Qur'an, who are not returned to decrepit age.
BAGHAWI:95:6/r5.anchor: عاصم الأحول عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس

BAGHAWI:95:6/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:6/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:95:6/r6.claim: Ghayr mamnūn means uncut off: the person's reward is recorded as the good they used to do.
BAGHAWI:95:6/r6.anchor: فلهم أجر غير ممنون } غير مقطوع

BAGHAWI:95:6/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:6/r7.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI:95:6/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the reward comes without further deeds.

BAYDAWI:95:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:95:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:95:6/r1.claim: The exception of believers who do good deeds is a disconnected exception.
BAYDAWI:95:6/r1.anchor: فيكون قوله( إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ) استثناء منقطعا

BAYDAWI:95:6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:95:6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:95:6/r2.anchor: ( فلهم أجر غير ممنون ) لا ينقطع

BAYDAWI:95:6/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:95:6/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:95:6/r3.claim: Alternatively, no one will hold the reward over them as a favor.

BAYDAWI:95:6/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:95:6/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:95:6/r4.claim: On the first sense of an unending reward, this clause establishes and confirms the result of the exception.
BAYDAWI:95:6/r4.anchor: وهو على الأولى حكم مرتب على الاستثناء مقرر له

BIQAI:95:6/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r1.claim: The prior judgment concerns most of humanity, while the righteous are a very small group and form the exception.
BIQAI:95:6/r1.anchor: ولما حكم بهذا الرد على جميع النوع

BIQAI:95:6/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r2.claim: Believers in God and His messengers have insight; divine gentleness lets reason, aided by original nature, overcome desire and protects them from decrepit old age.
BIQAI:95:6/r2.anchor: أي بالله ورسله فكانوا من ذوي البصائر والمعارف

BIQAI:95:6/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r3.claim: As age increases, their reason's light grows while desire and attachment to this world weaken and their spiritual insight strengthens.
BIQAI:95:6/r3.anchor: فكانوا كلما زدناهم سناً زدنا أنوار عقولهم ونقصنا نار شهواتهم بما أضعفنا من إحكام طبائعهم وتعلقهم بهذا العالم

BIQAI:95:6/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r4.claim: Good works confirm a true claim to faith and are beautiful deeds rooted in faith and perfected through divinely granted knowledge.
BIQAI:95:6/r4.anchor: من محاسن الأعمال من الأقوال والأفعال

BIQAI:95:6/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r5.claim: God preserves this small group on the original nature of the best form, keeping desire from tainting it, so they follow the messengers and embody justice, beneficence, and noble conduct.
BIQAI:95:6/r5.anchor: بما كملناهم به وشرفناهم على جميع الحيوانات

BIQAI:95:6/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r6.claim: The passage uses iḥtibāk: evil deeds and their punishment are implicit in the first clause, while preservation in the original fitra is implicit in the exception.
BIQAI:95:6/r6.anchor: فالآية كما ترى من الاحتباك : حذف أولاً

BIQAI:95:6/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r7.claim: Their reward is immense and lasts without interruption.
BIQAI:95:6/r7.anchor: وهو مع ذلك { غير ممنون * } أي مقطوع

BIQAI:95:6/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r8.claim: Alternatively, God does not hold the reward over them as a favor, even in illness or old age.
BIQAI:95:6/r8.anchor: أو يمن عليهم به حتى في حالة المرض والهرم

BIQAI:95:6/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r9.claim: They sincerely resolve never to omit a good deed; when old age makes them unable, they still receive the reward for what they did in health.
BIQAI:95:6/r9.anchor: وعزموا عزماً صادقاً أنهم لا ينقصون من أعمال البر ذرة

BIQAI:95:6/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r10.claim: The reward answers their actions, yet both its basis and its extension are God's grace; those who follow desire downward face great punishment.
BIQAI:95:6/r10.anchor: فضلاً منه بالأصل والفرع حتى أنهم إذا عجزوا بالهرم

DURR:95:6/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:6/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:95:6/r1.claim: Abu Musa reports that the Prophet said a servant committed to good receives the same record of deeds when illness or travel interrupts him; he recited this verse.
DURR:95:6/r1.anchor: عن أبي موسى قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا كان العبد على طريقة من الخير فمرض أو سافر كتب الله له مثل ما كان يعمل

DURR:95:6/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:6/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:95:6/r2.claim: The Prophet says that illness or travel earns a servant the reward of what he did while healthy and resident.
DURR:95:6/r2.anchor: عن أبي موسى قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا مرض العبد أو سافر كتب الله له من الأجر مثل ما كان يعمل صحيحاً مقيماً

DURR:95:6/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:6/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:95:6/r3.claim: The right-hand angel continues recording good deeds when weakness prevents them, while the left-hand angel withholds sins; the report also says Qur'an reciters escape decrepit age.
DURR:95:6/r3.anchor: عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله : { فلهم أجر غير ممنون } قال : «غير ممنون ما يكتب لهم صاحب اليمين

DURR:95:6/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:6/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:95:6/r4.claim: When a servant becomes ill, the left-hand angel is told to stop recording and the right-hand angel to record his best habitual deeds.
DURR:95:6/r4.anchor: عن مكحول قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا مرض العبد يقال لصاحب الشمال : ارفع عنه القلم

DURR:95:6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:6/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:95:6/r5.claim: A believer who praises God through affliction rises sinless, and God orders that his prior healthy deeds continue to be credited.
DURR:95:6/r5.anchor: عن شداد بن أوس : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : «إذا ابتليت عبداً من عبادي مؤمناً فحمدني على ما ابتليته

IBNASHUR:95:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:6/r1.claim: The exception is connected to the general category of humanity; the remaining nonbelievers stay in the lowest state.
IBNASHUR:95:6/r1.anchor: استثناء متصل من عموم الإِنسان فلما أخبر عن الإِنسان بأنه ردّ أسفل سافلين ثم استثني من عمومه الذين آمنوا بقي غير المؤمنين في أسفل سافلين

IBNASHUR:95:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:6/r2.claim: People who believed after sinking into idolatry return to the natural disposition God gave humanity and thus recover its original best form.
IBNASHUR:95:6/r2.anchor: أن الذين آمنوابعد أن ردوا أسفل سافلين أيام الإِشراك صاروا بالإِيمان إلى الفطرة التي فطر الله الإِنسان عليها

IBNASHUR:95:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:6/r3.claim: After revelation of the law, good works deepen the natural disposition, improve character, and lead to further virtues; the phrase praises faith as the motive for believers' conduct at revelation.
IBNASHUR:95:6/r3.anchor: لأن عمل الصالحات من أحسن التقويم بعد مجيء الشريعة لأنها تزيد الفطرة رسوخاً وينسحب الإِيمان على الأخلاق

IBNASHUR:95:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:6/r4.claim: He cites the hadith that the Prophet was sent to perfect noble character as support for the role of righteous deeds in moral refinement; no grading is given.
IBNASHUR:95:6/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث : « إنما بعثت لأتمم مكارم الأخلاق »

IBNASHUR:95:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:6/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:6/r5.claim: The good-works phrase is an explanatory descriptive attribute praising believers rather than a restrictive condition.
IBNASHUR:95:6/r5.anchor: فكان عطف { وعملوا الصالحات } للثناء على المؤمنين بأن إيمانهم باعث لهم على العمل الصالح

IBNASHUR:95:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:6/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:6/r6.claim: An interrupted exception is impossible here because the فـ in فلهم excludes that parsing.
IBNASHUR:95:6/r6.anchor: وليس لانقطاع الاستثناء هنا احتمال لأن وجود الفاء في قوله : { فلهم أجر غير ممنون } يأباه كل الإِبايَة

IBNASHUR:95:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:6/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:6/r7.claim: The reward announces further favor beyond the exception's implication that believers are not among the lowest; the indefinite أجر magnifies it.
IBNASHUR:95:6/r7.anchor: وفُرع على معنى الاستثناء وهو أنهم ليسوا ممن يرد أسفل سافلين الإِخبارُ بأن لهم أجراً عظيماً

IBNASHUR:95:6/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:6/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:6/r8.claim: غير ممنون can mean a reward not tainted by the recipient being reminded or reproached for receiving it.
IBNASHUR:95:6/r8.anchor: والممنون : الذي يُمنّ على المأجُور به ، أي لهم أجر لا يشوبه كدر

IBNASHUR:95:6/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:6/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:6/r9.claim: Alternatively, ممنون derives from cutting a rope and means cut off or near to being cut off.
IBNASHUR:95:6/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفعولاً من مَنَّ الحبلَ ، إذا قطعه فهو منين ، أي مقطوع أو موشك على التقطع

IBNATIYYA:95:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r1.claim: Even if some believers experience decline in this life, they will have an undiminished reward in the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r1.anchor: ثم أخبر أن { الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات } وإن نال بعضهم هذا في الدنيا { فلهم } في الآخرة { أجر غير ممنون }

IBNATIYYA:95:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r2.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد وأبو العالية
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Qatāda, Ibn Zayd, and Abū al-ʿĀliya interpret the return to the lowest as the unbeliever’s fall into Hell; the exception is disconnected, so believers are not cast there for disbelief.
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد وأبو العالية : المعنى { رددناه أسفل سافلين } في النار على كفره ، ثم استثنى { الذين آمنوا } استثناء منفصلا

IBNATIYYA:95:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r3.claim: Anas reports the Prophet: God eases a believer’s reckoning from 50, grants repentance at 60, love in heaven at 70, records good and overlooks sins at 80, forgives and enables intercession at 90, then credits lifelong practice at 100.
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r3.anchor: وفي حديث عن أنس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا بلغ المؤمن خمسين سنة خفف الله تعالى حسابه

IBNATIYYA:95:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r4.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet that when a believer is returned to the weakest age, God records the best he did in strength; the passage connects this to an unending reward.
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r4.anchor: وفي حديث «إن المؤمن إذا رد إلى أرذل العمر كتب الله له خير ما كان يعمله في قوته ، وذلك أجر غير ممنون

IBNATIYYA:95:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r5.claim: A long report from ʿIkrima, not raised to the Prophet, likewise says those returned to extreme old age receive reward like what they did in health and youth.
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r5.anchor: وفي لفظ قال: من رد منهم إلى أرذل العمر جرى له من الأجر

IBNATIYYA:95:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r6.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r6.claim: Mujāhid and others explain ممنون as counted or diminished, or as a reward for which beneficiaries are made to feel indebted; the note glosses reduction as diminishing the reward.
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r6.anchor: و { ممنون } معناه : محسوب مصَرِّد{[11895]} يمن عليهم ، قاله مجاهد

IBNATIYYA:95:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r7.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r7.claim: Many exegetes explain ممنون as uncut or uninterrupted, from the expression for a weak, broken cord.
IBNATIYYA:95:6/r7.anchor: وقال كثير من المفسرين : معناه مقطوع من قولهم حبل منين ، أي ضعيف منقطع

MAWARDI:95:6/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:6/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:95:6/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas understands the reward as undiminished; the cited anonymous poem uses غير ممنون in this sense.
MAWARDI:95:6/r1.anchor:
غير منقوص ،   قاله ابن عباس ،   وقال الشاعر :
يا عين جودي بدمع غير ممنون

MAWARDI:95:6/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:6/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:95:6/r2.claim: Mujahid says the reward is not reckoned or counted.

MAWARDI:95:6/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:6/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:95:6/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the reward is not spoiled by reproach or injury.
MAWARDI:95:6/r3.anchor: الثالث : غير مكدر بالمن والأذى ،   قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI:95:6/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:6/r4.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI:95:6/r4.claim: Ibn ʿIsa understands the reward as uninterrupted.
MAWARDI:95:6/r4.anchor: الرابع : غير مقطوع ،   قاله ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI:95:6/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:6/r5.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:95:6/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets it as reward granted without the corresponding deed.
MAWARDI:95:6/r5.anchor: الخامس : أجر بغير عمل ،   قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI:95:6/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:6/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:95:6/r6.claim: An unattributed report says that one who reaches old age is credited with the good works he can no longer perform.
MAWARDI:95:6/r6.anchor: وحكي أن من بلغ الهرم كتب له أجر ما عجز عنه من العمل الصالح

MAWARDI:95:6/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:6/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI:95:6/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud says that what each person does in old age does not harm him.
MAWARDI:95:6/r7.anchor: السادس : أن لا يضر كل أحد منهم ما عمله في كبره ،   قاله ابن مسعود .

NASAFI:95:6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:95:6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:95:6/r1.claim: Unlike Surat al-Inshiqaq, this verse includes the fāʾ to combine two linguistic constructions.
NASAFI:95:6/r1.anchor: ودخل الفاء هنا دون سورة الانشقاق للجمع بين اللغتين

NASAFI:95:6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:95:6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:95:6/r2.claim: The exception is connected under the first explanation and disconnected under the second; for the disconnected reading it means 'but' those who were righteous among the aged and infirm.
NASAFI:95:6/r2.anchor: والاستثناء على الأول متصل ،   وعلى الثاني منقطع ،   أي ولكن الذين كانوا صالحين من الهرمى والزمنى

NASAFI:95:6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:95:6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:95:6/r3.claim: The aged and infirm who remained righteous receive unending reward for obedience, patience in the trials of old age, bearing hardships, and worship.
NASAFI:95:6/r3.anchor: فلهم ثواب غير منقطع على طاعتهم وصبرهم على الابتلاء بالشيخوخة والهرم ،   وعلى مقاساة المشاق والقيام بالعبادة .

QURTUBI:95:5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:95:5/r8.claim: The exception in the following verse is connected if أسفل سافلين means Hell, but disconnected if it means senility.
QURTUBI:95:5/r8.anchor: والاستثناء على قول من قال  " أسفل سافلين "  النار ،   متصل .   ومن قال : إنه الهرم فهو منقطع .

QURTUBI:95:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:6/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:95:6/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says believers have their good deeds recorded and bad deeds erased; those who reach old age are not held liable for what they do in decrepitude.
QURTUBI:95:6/r1.anchor: قاله ابن عباس .   قال : وهم الذين أدركهم الكبر ،   لا يؤاخذون بما عملوه في كبرهم .

QURTUBI:95:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:6/r2.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI:95:6/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reports from Ibn Abbas that when youthful worship and charity diminish through age-related weakness, God continues to credit the deeds the person used to perform.
QURTUBI:95:6/r2.anchor: وروى الضحاك عنه قال : إذا كان العبد في شبابه كثير الصلاة كثير الصيام والصدقة ،

QURTUBI:95:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:6/r3.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI:95:6/r3.claim: The Prophet says that when a servant travels or becomes ill, God records for him the same deeds he performed while resident and healthy.
QURTUBI:95:6/r3.anchor: وفي حديث قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : [ إذا سافر العبد أو مرض كتب الله له مثل ما كان يعمل مقيما صحيحا ] .

QURTUBI:95:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:6/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:95:6/r4.claim: Another view says a knowledgeable person acting on knowledge neither becomes senile nor loses his reason in old age.
QURTUBI:95:6/r4.anchor: وقيل :  " إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات "  فإنه لا يخرف ولا يهرم{[16193]} ،   ولا يذهب عقل

QURTUBI:95:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:6/r5.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI:95:6/r5.claim: Ikrima says that whoever recites the Qur’an is not returned to the most decrepit age.
QURTUBI:95:6/r5.anchor: وعن عاصم الأحول عن عكرمة قال : من قرأ القرآن لم يرد إلى أرذل العمر .

QURTUBI:95:6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:6/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI:95:6/r6.claim: A report from Ibn Umar attributes to the Prophet the saying: blessed is the person whose life is long and whose deeds are good.
QURTUBI:95:6/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : [ طوبى لمن طال عمره وحسن عمله ] .

QURTUBI:95:6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:95:6/r7.claim: A report says that after a believer dies, God commands his two angels to worship at his grave until the Resurrection and records that worship for him.
QURTUBI:95:6/r7.anchor: وروي : إن العبد المؤمن إذا مات أمر اللّه ملكيه{[16194]} أن يتعبدا على قبره إلى يوم القيامة ،   ويكتب له ذلك .

QURTUBI:95:6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:6/r8.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI:95:6/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the reward as being granted without further deeds.
QURTUBI:95:6/r8.anchor: " فلهم أجر غير ممنون "  قال الضحاك : أجر بغير عمل .

QURTUBI:95:6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:6/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:95:6/r9.claim: Another explanation takes غير ممنون to mean an uninterrupted reward.

RAZI:95:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:95:6/r1.claim: On the first preceding interpretation, the exception is disconnected: rather, righteous elderly people receive lasting reward for obedience, patience in God's trial of aging, endured hardship, and worship despite weakened movement.
RAZI:95:6/r1.anchor: على القول الأول منقطع ، والمعنى ولكن الذين كانوا صالحين من الهرمى فلهم ثواب دائم على طاعتهم وصبرهم على ابتلاء الله

RAZI:95:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:6/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:95:6/r2.claim: On the second preceding interpretation, the exception is straightforwardly connected.
RAZI:95:6/r2.anchor: وأما على القول الثاني فالاستثناء متصل ظاهر الاتصال

RAZI:95:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:6/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:95:6/r3.claim: One explanation of غير ممنون is that the reward is neither diminished nor cut off.

RAZI:95:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:6/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:95:6/r4.claim: Another explanation is that no one reminds the recipients of the reward as a favor.

RAZI:95:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:6/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:95:6/r5.claim: Both readings describe the reward: it must endure without interruption and remain free from the humiliation of reproach.
RAZI:95:6/r5.anchor: لأنه يجب أن يكون غير منقطع وأن لا يكون منغصا بالمنة

TAB:95:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r1.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB:95:6/r1.claim: Some exegetes call this a connected exception from the preceding phrase: singular “the human” denotes the human species collectively, as in the Sūrat al-ʿAṣr statement that humanity is in loss except believers who do good.
TAB:95:6/r1.anchor: فقال بعضهم : هو استثناء صحيح من قوله ( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ ) قالوا : وإنما جاز استثناء الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

TAB:95:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r2.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB:95:6/r2.claim: On that analysis, the generic singular can take a plural exception, and the comparative superlative can be construed with a plural group.
TAB:95:6/r2.anchor: قالوا : وكذلك جاز أن يقال : ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ فيضاف أفعل إلى جماعة

TAB:95:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:95:6/r3.claim: A saying attributed to ʿIkrima says a Qurʾān reciter will not be returned to decrepit age; he cites the passage and explains the decline as reaching a state of knowing nothing after knowledge.
TAB:95:6/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة ، قال : ( كان يقال ) : من قرأ القرآنلم يُردّ إلى أرذل العمر

TAB:95:6/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB:95:6/r4.claim: Others say believers too may reach decrepit age; the exception is from an implied result: their reason and work fail, but the reward for good deeds done while healthy continues.
TAB:95:6/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات قد يدخلون في الذين رُدّوا إلى أَسْفَل سافلين ، لأن أرذْل العُمر قد يردّ إليه المؤمن والكافر

TAB:95:6/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r5.speaker: author
TAB:95:6/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī allows that the exception could be disconnected: believers receive their promised reward even after being returned to the lowest state.
TAB:95:6/r5.anchor: وقد يُحتمل أن يكون قوله : ( إلاّ الّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ ) استثناء منقطعا ، لأنه يحسن أن يقال : ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين

TAB:95:6/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:95:6/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a person who did good while young and strong keeps receiving its reward until death when age makes him unable to continue.
TAB:95:6/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس ( إلاّ الّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ فَلَهُمْ أجْرٌ غَيرُ مَمْنُونِ ) قال : فأيّما رجل كان يعمل

TAB:95:6/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:95:6/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says an obedient believer’s good deeds from youth remain credited after senility, and he is not held to account for acts done after losing his reason.
TAB:95:6/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ( لاّ الّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ فَلَهُمْ أجْرٌ غَيرُ مَمْنُونٍ ) يقول : إذا كان يعمل

TAB:95:6/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r8.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB:95:6/r8.claim: Ibrāhīm says a believer who reaches decrepit age is credited with the best level of work he performed in youth and health.
TAB:95:6/r8.anchor: عن إبراهيم ، في قوله : ( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ ) قال : إلى أرذل العمر ، فإذا بلغ المؤمن إلى أرذل العمر

TAB:95:6/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:95:6/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says senile believers are not blamed for what they do after reason is gone; their prior obedience in youth grounds their preserved reward.
TAB:95:6/r9.anchor: عن أبي رَزِين ، عن ابن عباس ( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ إلاّ الّذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ) قال : هم الذين أدركهم الكِبرَ

TAB:95:6/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r10.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:95:6/r10.claim: ʿIkrima says God will fully give the person his reward or deeds and will not hold him accountable when returned to decrepit age.
TAB:95:6/r10.anchor: سُئل عكِرمة ، عن قوله : ( إلاّ الّذين آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ فَلَهُمْ أجْرٌ غَيرُ مَمْنُونٍ ) قال : يوفيه الله أجره أو عمله

TAB:95:6/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r11.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:95:6/r11.claim: ʿIkrima also says extreme old age does not harm the elderly man if God lets him end with his best former deeds.
TAB:95:6/r11.anchor: عن عكرِمة ( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ إلاّ الّذين آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ ) قال : الشيخ الهَرِم لم يضرّه كبره

TAB:95:6/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r12.speaker: قتادة
TAB:95:6/r12.claim: Qatāda says a person who practiced righteousness before senility receives the same reward he received while able to work.
TAB:95:6/r12.anchor: عن قتادة ( إلاّ الّذين آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ ) قال : من أدركه الهرم ، وكان يعمل صالحا ، كان له مثل أجره

TAB:95:6/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r13.speaker: آخرون
TAB:95:6/r13.claim: Another group instead understands the previous phrase as descent into Hell and treats believers who do good as a connected exception from those sent there.
TAB:95:6/r13.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل معنى ذلك : ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين في جهنم ، إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ، فلهم أجر غير ممنون ، فعلى هذا التأويل

TAB:95:6/r14.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r14.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:95:6/r14.claim: Mujāhid glosses the exception in the Hell interpretation as “except whoever believes.”
TAB:95:6/r14.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ، عن مجاهد ( ثُمّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ إلاّ الّذِينَ آمَنُوا ) : إلا من آمن .

TAB:95:6/r15.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r15.speaker: الحسن
TAB:95:6/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the Hell reading makes this exception parallel to the exception for believers in Sūrat al-ʿAṣr.
TAB:95:6/r15.anchor: قال الحسن : هي كقوله : ( وَالْعَصْر إنّ الإنْسانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ إلا الّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ )

TAB:95:6/r16.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r16.speaker: author
TAB:95:6/r16.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the old-age reading: believers who did good while healthy and young retain, after senility, the reward they earned while strong enough to act.
TAB:95:6/r16.anchor: قول من قال : معناه : ثم رددناه إلى أرذل العمر ، إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات في حال صحتهم وشبابهم

TAB:95:6/r17.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:95:6/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “unminished reward” as reward that is not reduced.
TAB:95:6/r17.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : ( فَلَهُمْ أجْرٌ غَيرُ مَمْنُونِ ) يقول : غير منقوص .

TAB:95:6/r18.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r18.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:95:6/r18.claim: Mujāhid interprets the reward as uncounted; Ibrāhīm gives the same explanation in reports cited by al-Ṭabarī.
TAB:95:6/r18.anchor: عن مجاهد ( فَلَهُمْ أجْرٌ غَيرُ مَمْنُونٍ ) : غير محسوب .

TAB:95:6/r19.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r19.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB:95:6/r19.claim: Ibrāhīm also explains the reward as uncounted.
TAB:95:6/r19.anchor: عن إبراهيم ( فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ ) قال : غير محسوب .

TAB:95:6/r20.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r20.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:95:6/r20.claim: An additional reported gloss takes the phrase to mean an uncut, uninterrupted reward.
TAB:95:6/r20.anchor: وقد قيل : إن معنى ذلك : فلهم أجر غير مقطوع .

TAB:95:6/r21.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:6/r21.speaker: author
TAB:95:6/r21.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers “not diminished,” like the reward of healthy youth; he relates this to manīn, something weak, and cites poetry about giving without minning or excess to convey no diminution or flaw.
TAB:95:6/r21.anchor: وهو عندي من قولهم : جبل مَنِين : إذا كان ضعيفا ، ومنه قول الشاعر : أعْطَوْا هُنَيْدَةَ يَحْدُوها ثَمَانِيَةٌ *** ما فِي عَطائِهِمُ مَنّ وَلا سَرَفُ
